text: María Fernanda Cabal Molina (born August 8, 1966) is a Colombian political scientist, businesswoman, politician, and Senator of Colombia. A member of the Democratic Center Party, she has held her seat since 2018 and is the party's most voted-for member of Congress. Born in Cali, Cauca Valley, she lived there until her high school years before moving to Bogotá, D.C., where she graduated from the University of the Andes and joined the Political Science Department as coordinator of the Democracy Program, funded by the National Endowment for Democracy. She began her political career as a Member of the Chamber of Representatives in 2014 and was first elected to the Senate in 2018, being re-elected in 2022. Cabal is a female member of the Democratic Center and holds the highest-ranking position in the Senate. She is known for her far-right views and was one of the members of her party who voted against the plebiscite for the peace process. She is of Spanish ancestry from Asturias and Madrid. During the 1990s, she participated in the student movement that later promoted the Seventh Ballot, calling for constitutional reform through the convening of the National Constituent Assembly. Although baptized under the Catholic rite by her parents in 1964, she identifies as a Lapsed Catholic and has expressed admiration for the Evangelical Protestant rite, attending services on multiple occasions. Cabal is known for her conservative positions and has maintained close relations with the Donald Trump administration in the United States and Jair Bolsonaro of Brazil, while consistently criticizing leftist movements in Colombia and Latin America. She supports controversial policies, including the right of civilians to bear arms for self-defense and the rejection of the peace agreement between the FARC guerrillas and the Colombian government. She also signed the Madrid Charter of the Madrid Forum, joining the right-wing group organized by the Spanish political party Vox.
